item.title: Re: Tag Thread 3: Revenge of the Tags
item.content:encoded:
Denied.

This tag is not a goi, character, or attribute. It instead signifies the presence of an author's formatting choices. Threat levels are not officially recognized, unlike object classes (which appear in How To Write An SCP for instance).

Additionally when making tag requests, you must provide the initial list of pages which meet the criteria for the proposed tag so they can be applied, if approved.

item.title: Re: Tag Request - Pataphysics
item.content:encoded:
Denied — per an earlier comment by DrMagnus

After reading through a decent number of these examples, most of them are covered neatly by the meta tag.

Beyond that, I'm loath to create a new attribute tag that is already covered by a broader category, especially as "pataphysical" doesn't really add that much of a spin over 'meta'. I'm very much against creating narrower tags without significant benefit.

I will admit that there's definitely a case to be made on this one, but the benefit of 'pataphysical' over 'meta' are slim in my mind, and is just going to lead to one of the tags getting orphaned or disused.

I'm open to a counter argument in reply.

Additionally, the broad nature of the tag, in conjugation with the application over both SCPs and non-SCPs, would make the issue of tagging too ambiguous.

item.title: Re: Tag Thread 3: Revenge of the Tags
item.content:encoded:
I probably ought to mention it since I see it here (it's relevant, even if it's not the right forum)—

A list of pages that use the Void format would be better served by looking at the backlinks of Void Post Template. However, few pages that use the Void format use that component, so I'll ask the authors of Void articles if they'd like to switch to it.

There's some functionality that the Void Post Template doesn't have. Namely, (1) the ability to put images inside the Void Post, and (2) parent/child replies. I can probably code it to facilitate #1, but #2 is not currently something I can add. I know lacking these functions might make the Void Post Template unattractive for the other authors who have used Void Posts in their articles (especially those who came up with it and included extra "features"), but, the ability to mock up special replies with regular, non-component divs can still be achieved.

item.title: Tag Thread 3: Revenge of the Tags
item.content:encoded:
Greetings skippers.

This here fancy new thread is the new place to propose tags!

Why do we have a new thread?
The will of magnus!

So, the old old thread was six pages and now the new thread was six pages, and it's still difficult to find older posts about tags that were denied.

Frankly, it drives me apeshit, and that's enough to warrant a new thread. Not much changes for the users, but it makes it significantly easier on staff.

How to use this thread

If you would like to suggest a tag, please provide the following in a NEW POST. Replies to this post, or any other suggestion post will not be actioned, and will probably make me whinge at you.

Your post should have the title of:
"Tag Request — tag-name-goes-here"

Please provide within the post the following:

  • Articles proving it qualifies
  • Justification if it requires it

If you would like to provide multiple suggestions, please separate them with ----- a line divider.

Q. Okay, so what happens then?
A. A technical team member OS or higher will approve or dissaprove your tag. After that, they'll tag the articles you provided justification for, add the tag to the tag list on O5 command.

Q. What if I disagree with your justification?
A. Post a reply to the original post, explaining your position. A followup post will be made by the approver, or myself.

Q. What if you still deny it, after appealing?
A. Then thems the breaks. Sorry >.>

Q. How long will the decision take?
A. Depends on my, and the tag team's workload.

Q. Did you seriously copy and paste the starting post?
A. Yup. Tough nuggets.
